column1: # THE SOURCES SENTENCE, AS DATA — CLAIM-1's left-hand side (D239 §5, helm ruling 2026-09-13).
# `README.md`'s "It is built from public sources only: …" sentence is RENDERED from this
# table by `scripts/check_source_roles.py`, which also checks each row's claim against the
# TREE.  ⛔ The rendering is TRANSPORT ONLY: a byte-for-byte re-derivation proves the file
# matches its generator and says NOTHING about whether the generator tells the truth.  The
# CLAIM column is what carries the load.
# ⛔ THE TABLE IS THE POPULATION OF THE SENTENCE, NOT OF THE MODELS.  Five things are named
# and D239 §3's three roles cover only the SEMANTICS ones; the SDM is a DOCUMENT and XED is a
# DECODER.  Every row therefore carries a KIND, and every row states a claim the tree can be
# asked about — or says NONE, in the table, rather than by omission.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated):
#   name    the thing, as the sentence names it
#   kind    SEMANTICS | DOCUMENT | DECODER
#   role    for SEMANTICS: EXECUTED | READ-MECHANICALLY | NAMED-AS-INTENT   (D239 §3)
#           for every other kind: the claim's short name, or NONE
#   claim   the checker key in check_source_roles.py that derives this row from the tree
#   phrase  the row's text inside the rendered sentence
# ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-09-13 WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, because a name grep is not a code path:
# `Sail` occurs in exactly TWO script lines and both are prose (a positioning-table column
# header and a comment); no Sail artifact is vendored and nothing reads one.  The same
# word-bounded matcher finds `x86isa` in 16 script files.  ⇒ NAMED-AS-INTENT is DERIVED here,
# not assumed from the sentence that already says it.
# ⚠️ AND `XED` HAS NO CONSUMED ARTIFACT EITHER — zero word-bounded mentions in any script, no
# `vendor/xed` — but it is NOT named-as-intent: `Main.lean` writes `XED (trusted)` into every
# coverage-table row, so its claim is RECORDED DECODE TRUST, checkable against the generated
# table.  That is a third kind of claim, and it is why a two-valued EXECUTED/NOT gate could
# not have expressed this sentence.
# 📌 SCOPE OF THE CLOSURE CHECK, STATED SO THE EXCLUSION IS NOT SILENT: closure (iii) is over
# the models the DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS INVOKES.  `vendor/liblisa` is vendored and read by
# `scripts/liblisa_hardware_check.py`, and it is deliberately NOT a row: it is a one-off
# hardware ground-truth check, not a source the model is built from, and the harness does not
# invoke it.  ⚠️ It is named here rather than omitted, because an exclusion nobody wrote down
# is indistinguishable from an oversight — and if the sentence ever claims hardware
# corroboration, this is the row that has to appear.
# 📌 FILED, NOT BUILT (D239 §5): an "independent-of" column.  The fleet map records that
# `sail-x86-from-acl2` is translated from ACL2 and that K does not decode machine bytes, so
# agreement with Sail would test the TRANSLATOR.  Out of scope for this gate; the row shape
# accepts a further column without a migration.
